questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The differences between tea and coffee for health
How to make the perfect cup of coffee at home
Paying more for coffee that is fairer to farmers
Why coffee prices in shops keep going down each year
questions.why: They discuss the trend of paying more for ethically produced coffee and whether farmers benefit.

questions.q: How does Dan like his coffee?
options: Instant, with a little milk
Freshly ground and very strong
Black, with no sugar
From an expensive artisan café
questions.why: Dan says he's 'an instant coffee kind of guy' and likes it with a dash of milk.

questions.q: What kind of coffee does Catherine prefer?
options: Cheap instant coffee
Weak coffee with lots of milk
Any coffee, as long as it wakes her up
Dark, strong coffee made from fresh beans
questions.why: She prefers freshly-ground beans and likes her coffee dark and strong, maybe Colombian or Brazilian.

questions.q: Would Catherine pay more if the farmer got a fairer price?
options: No, she already pays too much
Yes, because she thinks it matters
Only if the coffee tasted better
She isn't sure
questions.why: She says she would, 'because I think that that sort of thing is important'.

questions.q: What did the UN report look at?
options: How much coffee customers in Western countries drink
How processing, branding and marketing affect farmers
Which countries grow the best-tasting coffee beans
Why artisan cafes in big cities are closing down
questions.why: The report observed the effect of smarter processing, branding and marketing on farmers and their communities.

questions.q: According to Dan, who takes most of the profits from coffee?
options: The farmers who grow it
The big supermarkets
The owners of cafes
The roasting companies
questions.why: Dan says coffee is cheap until it's roasted, so 'roasters take most of the profits'.

questions.q: According to Jonathan Josephs, what happens when customers pay a premium?
options: The export price rises from $1.45 to $5.14 a pound
The roaster's price falls from $5 to $4 a pound
The farmer gets less money than before for each bag
Supermarkets sell more instant coffee to customers
questions.why: He says the roaster gets $17.45 and the export price also rises to $5.14, from $1.45.

questions.q: What does Catherine decide at the end?
options: To switch from coffee to tea for health reasons
To try the expensive Kopi luwak coffee next week
To look for ethically produced coffee from now on
To only drink cheap instant coffee at home like Dan
questions.why: She says she will definitely look for ethically produced coffee from now on.
